evidence_quotes: [Skip to content](#main) ![Goldberg Segalla logo](https://www.goldbergsegalla.com/app/uploads/2026/04/GS-Anniversary-Tagline-Horizonal-Logo-gray-and-red-1-1.svg) ![](https://www.goldbergsegalla.com/app/uploads/2023/07/NewsKnowledge_HEAD.jpg) # News & Knowledge 2025 Legionnaires’ Disease Community Cluster in New York City: Ongoing Public Health Investigation [Home](/) News & Knowledge Knowledge # 2025 Legionnaires’ Disease Community Cluster in New York City: Ongoing Public Health Investigation August 27, 2025 [Andrew J. Scholz](https://www.goldbergsegalla.com/our-team/andrew-j-scholz/) [Michael D. Shalhoub](https://www.goldbergsegalla.com/our-team/michael-d-shalhoub/) [Karen Cullinane](https://www.goldbergsegalla.com/our-team/karen-cullinane/) ## **Key Takeaways:** * ### The New York City Department of Health continues to investigate “a community cluster of Legionnaires’ disease” in the Central Harlem ZIP Codes of 10027, 10030, 10035, 10037 and 10039 * ### On August 26, the DOH reported more than 113 confirmed cases of the disease, with six deaths and seven people currently hospitalized * ### Litigation has reportedly already commenced; additional lawsuits are expected As has been widely reported by the media, in late July the New York City Department of Health (DOH) began “investigating a community cluster of Legionnaires’ disease in Central Harlem.” According to the [DOH website](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/legionnaires-disease.page), as of August 26 there have been over 113 confirmed cases of the disease. According to the DOH, six people had died and seven people were hospitalized as of that date. The DOH website outlines five ZIP Codes where the DOH is investigating: 10027, 10030, 10035, 10037 and 10039.

evidence_quotes: ![vaccineadvisor logo](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/logos/vaccineadvisor.svg) ![HMN logo](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/HMN-logo-1line.svg) ![facebook share](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/facebook-social-share.svg) ![twitter share](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/twitter-social-share-x.svg) ![linkedin share](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/linkedin-social-share.svg) ![email](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/email-social-share.svg) ![print](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/print-social-share.svg) # NYC Legionnaires’ Outbreak: Fourth Death Confirmed, 101 Sickened ![](https://www.vaccineadvisor.com/wp-content/themes/hm-advisor-child/assets/svg/key-point_icon.svg) HealthDay News — A Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in Central Harlem has now caused four deaths and sickened 101 people, New York City health officials confirmed. The bacteria that cause the illness, called *Legionella*, were found in 12 cooling towers across 10 buildings, including NYC Health + Hospitals/Harlem. Cooling towers help regulate temperature in large buildings, but if they are not cleaned properly, bacteria can grow and spread through mist in the air. “As of today, 11 of the 12 cooling towers in Central Harlem that tested positive for *Legionella* bacteria have completed remediation, and by tomorrow, all towers will have completed remediations,” New York City Mayor [Eric Adams](https://www.nyc.gov/office-of-the-mayor/bio.page) said on Aug. 14.
